description: Responses of the v1.7.0 RC1 candidate's frozen sidecar (snapstudio-api.exe) to the acceptance geometry fixtures. Synthetic 10x20x30 box; paths removed.

measured_against.verification_meaning: A physical machine of this kind answered these questions, read-only, and the answers were recorded.
measured_against.verification_note: Read read-only from a physical Snapmaker U1 on a LAN during the beta.23 and v0.7.x acceptance work.
known_unknowns: free storage on the printer — the firmware reports no sizes
how much filament is left on a loaded spool — the printer tracks which spool, not what remains

body.overall_text: By size, this model is small enough for the Snapmaker U1's bed, but the placement is a problem — see the placement finding below.

findings.text: By placement: 1 object falls outside the Snapmaker U1's plate, but the whole arrangement fits — moving it as one piece brings everything back on, keeping the creator's layout, rotation and scale.
findings.action: Move the arrangement onto the plate (Studio can save a corrected copy), or review the project in Snapmaker Orca.

fixes: Move the arrangement onto the plate (Studio can save a corrected copy), or review the project in Snapmaker Orca.

limitations: Studio checks only what it lists under “Studio checked.” It cannot know your slicer settings, how the filament has been stored, how clean or level the bed is, or how the printer behaves mid-print.
Studio does not slice. Verify in Snapmaker Orca before you print.
body.summary: Studio's checks did not flag anything in what they covered: design validation, colors against toolheads, first-layer risk. That is not a sign the print will succeed.
